Consulates ask for both; the copy is retained in the file. Passport should remain valid well beyond the 180-day visa validity and the intended residency period.

documents.name: Completed Mexican visa application form (Solicitud de Visa Mexicana)
documents.description: The SRE visa application form, printed, completed and signed, presented at the consular interview. Some consulates provide their own current-year version of the form — download it from the specific consulate holding your appointment.

documents.name: One recent color passport-style photograph of the applicant
documents.description: A single recent color photo, front view, white background, face fully visible and uncovered, without glasses. Some consulates specify a size close to 3.9 cm x 3.1 cm rather than U.S. passport dimensions — confirm exact size with your consulate, as this varies.

documents.name: Twelve consecutive original monthly bank or investment account statements (savings route)
documents.description: Economic solvency option (a): original personal bank or investment statements for the last 12 months showing a month-end balance above the UMA-based threshold (roughly USD $69,000–$74,000 in 2025–2026 consular sheets; the exact peso figure is set per consulate and per exchange rate on your appointment date). Digital-banking users must bring statements stamped by a bank branch — plain home printouts are rejected.

documents.name: Six months of pension/salary payment receipts with matching bank statements (income route)
documents.description: Economic solvency option (b), used instead of the savings route: six most recent pay stubs, SSA award/benefit statements or pension receipts showing net monthly income above the threshold (approximately USD $4,300–$4,500 per month in 2026), accompanied by the six matching bank statements showing the direct deposits. Some consulates also require an employment letter.

documents.name: Consular appointment confirmation (citas.sre.gob.mx / MiConsulado booking)
documents.description: Printed or digital confirmation of the individual visa appointment — one appointment per applicant, including each dependent. Must be booked at a Mexican consulate in the United States; jurisdiction rules and document expectations differ by consulate.

documents.name: Receipt for the non-refundable consular visa processing fee
documents.description: Proof of payment of the visa application fee (around USD $54 in current consular sheets), paid by credit or debit card (Visa/Mastercard) at the consulate; some posts also accept cash. The fee is not refunded if the visa is denied.

documents.name: Certified marriage certificate or birth certificate proving the family bond (dependent applicants only)
documents.description: Required only when applying through family unity or bringing dependents: certified copy of the marriage certificate (spouse) or original birth certificate (child/parent). U.S.- and Mexico-issued civil documents are accepted directly; documents from any other country need apostille/legalization plus certified Spanish translation.

documents.name: Apostille and certified Spanish translation for non-U.S., non-Mexican documents
documents.description: Any supporting document not issued in the United States or Mexico must carry an apostille or legalization from the issuing country, and documents drafted in a language other than Spanish or English must include an official translation. Verify with your specific consulate, as translation policies differ between posts.

documents.name: Temporary resident visa sticker affixed in the passport
documents.description: The physical visa foil issued by the consulate after approval. It is valid for a maximum of 180 days from issuance and authorizes a single entry to Mexico to begin the residency exchange — it is not the residency itself.

documents.name: Entry immigration form (FMM) endorsed by the officer as 'CANJE — 30 días'
documents.description: At the port of entry the immigration officer must record your admission as a canje (exchange) with 30 days, not as a tourist stay. Check this at the counter and ask for correction if mismarked; an incorrectly marked entry record is a common cause of failed card applications. Keep a physical and digital copy.

documents.name: INM canje appointment with Número Único de Trámite (NUT)
documents.description: Register the 'Expedición de documento migratorio por canje' request on the INM Micrositio de Trámites Migratorios to obtain a NUT, then book the in-person appointment at the INM office covering your address. The appointment must fall within 30 calendar days of entry; where possible arrange it before leaving the U.S.

documents.name: INM 'Formato Básico' and printed, signed canje application
documents.description: The INM basic data format plus the trámite request form for the canje, downloaded from the INM site, completed, printed and signed, and handed in at the appointment together with the rest of the file.

documents.name: Bank-stamped proof of payment of INM derechos (hoja de ayuda / SAT formato e5)
documents.description: Print the payment sheet, pay at an authorized bank branch (e.g. BBVA, Banorte, Santander) or by Visa/Mastercard at the INM office, and bring the stamped receipt. INM does not accept cash, and home-printed SPEI transfer confirmations are not valid proof. Card issuance fees rose substantially under the November 2025 fee schedule.

documents.name: Biometric enrolment record at INM (photograph, signature, fingerprints)
documents.description: At the canje appointment INM captures your photo, signature and fingerprints in person; no self-supplied photos substitute for this step. There is no document to bring, but attendance is mandatory and the record is what generates your card and CURP.

documents.name: Proof of Mexican address (comprobante de domicilio)
documents.description: A recent utility bill or signed lease in your name or your host's name, used to confirm the INM office with jurisdiction over you and later required by banks and RENAPO. Not listed on the federal canje requirement sheet — verify with your local INM office, as practice varies by delegation.

documents.name: Tarjeta de Residente Temporal (physical residency card)
documents.description: The plastic card issued by INM after the canje, valid initially for one year and renewable up to a four-year total. It carries your NUE and your 18-character CURP printed on the front, and is your primary Mexican ID for banking, leases and travel re-entry.

documents.name: Printed CURP certificate from the RENAPO portal
documents.description: Although the CURP is generated automatically when INM issues your resident card, banks and government offices require the free letter-size printout downloaded from the official RENAPO/gob.mx CURP portal. Check the spelling of your name and date of birth immediately; corrections must be made in person at a RENAPO module with your passport and resident card.

documents.name: RFC registration with SAT (Mexican tax ID)
documents.description: Needed if you will earn Mexican-source income, invoice clients, buy property or take formal employment; not needed by most solvency-based residents living on foreign income. Requires your CURP, resident card and proof of address.

documents.name: INM renewal application filed at least 30 days before card expiry
documents.description: Temporary resident cards are renewed for 1 or 3 additional years, using an updated file plus a new derechos payment. Start the renewal before the current card expires — lapsing into irregular status triggers fines and can block future trámites. Note that solvency-based residents who wish to work in Mexico must separately request work authorization from INM.

documents.name: Change-of-condition file for permanent residency after four years
documents.description: To convert to Residente Permanente, INM requires the passport or travel document used to obtain temporary residence, a still-valid temporary resident card, proof of payment of the change-of-condition fee, and evidence of the qualifying ground. Time spent as a student temporary resident does not count toward the four years.

documents.name: National visa application form (Solicitud de visado nacional)
documents.description: Official long-stay national visa form, completed in full and signed by each applicant (a separate form for each accompanying family member). Submitted in person at the Spanish Consulate General covering your UK place of residence (London, Manchester or Edinburgh).

documents.name: Valid UK passport plus photocopy of the biometric data page
documents.description: Original passport with minimum 1 year validity remaining and at least two blank pages; passports issued more than 10 years ago are not accepted. One photocopy of the biometric/data page(s) is submitted with the file. This is the document copy requirement, not the photo requirement.

documents.name: Recent passport-size colour photograph of the applicant
documents.description: One recent colour photo, light/plain background, full-face, no dark glasses, no glare and no head coverings obscuring the face oval. Separate and additional to the passport photocopy above.

documents.name: ACRO Police Certificate (UK criminal record certificate) with apostille
documents.description: For UK criminal records the Spanish consular network specifically requires the ACRO certificate. It must generally be under 6 months old at submission (unless the certificate states a different expiry), apostilled by the FCDO Legalisation Office and accompanied by an official Spanish translation. Certificates may also be required from any other country you lived in during the last 2–5 years.

documents.name: Declaración responsable of no criminal record (last 5 years)
documents.description: Signed sworn statement declaring the absence of any criminal record over the previous five years. This is a separate declaration from the ACRO certificate itself.

documents.name: FCDO apostille and sworn Spanish translation of all UK-issued documents
documents.description: Post-Brexit, UK public documents are no longer exempt from legalisation as EU documents are, so ACRO certificates, degrees, marriage/birth certificates etc. must be apostilled and, where applicable, translated into Spanish by an officially recognised (sworn) translator. Ask your consulate for its list of accepted translators, as practice varies by consulate.

documents.name: Employer or client certificate authorising remote work from Spain (minimum 3-month relationship)
documents.description: Letter/certificate from the non-Spanish employer or contracting company confirming the employment or commercial relationship has lasted at least 3 months at the date of application, and expressly permitting remote work from Spanish territory. Employees must also provide the employment contract containing the teleworking clause; freelancers must show contracts with clients where Spanish-based clients are no more than 20% of activity.

documents.name: Proof that the employing/contracting company has traded for at least one year
documents.description: Corporate documentation evidencing that the foreign company has been genuinely active for a minimum of one year — for a UK employer this is typically a Companies House certificate of incorporation plus a current filing/registry extract.
documents.source: Consulado General de España en Londres (Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, UE y Cooperación)

documents.name: Evidence of professional qualification or 3 years' relevant experience
documents.description: Either a university/higher-education or professional qualification (degree certificate, apostilled and translated) or documentation proving at least three years of experience in duties comparable to the telework role. If equivalence of a vocational qualification is doubtful, official recognition (convalidación) may be requested.

documents.name: Proof of sufficient income (200% of the Spanish minimum wage)
documents.description: Payslips, employment/service contracts and bank statements evidencing recurring income at or above 200% of the Spanish SMI (approximately €2,849/month in 2026), with uplifts of 75% of the SMI for the first dependent and 25% for each further dependent. Verify the current threshold with the consulate, as it changes each time the SMI is updated.

documents.name: Full private health insurance policy with an insurer authorised in Spain
documents.description: Certificate of cover from an insurer registered with the Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones, valid for the whole authorisation period, with no waiting periods, no co-payments and no coverage caps (100% of medical costs, including consultations, check-ups, illness and emergencies). A UK GHIC/EHIC or travel policy is not accepted.

documents.name: Social security undertaking plus UK A1 / Certificate of Coverage where applicable
documents.description: Declaración responsable committing to comply with social security obligations before starting the activity. If you remain in the UK system under the UK–EU social security coordination protocol, provide the HMRC A1/Certificate of Coverage; otherwise evidence of the company's registration with Spanish Social Security or your own affiliation.

documents.name: NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) request filed with the visa
documents.description: The consulate requires the NIE to be requested at the same time and in the same consular office as the digital nomad visa application. This is the identification number only — distinct from the physical TIE card obtained later in Spain.

documents.name: Proof of legal residence in the consular district and visa fee receipt
documents.description: Evidence that you legally reside in the UK area covered by the consulate where you apply (e.g. UK council tax bill, tenancy agreement or utility bill), together with proof of payment of the consular visa fee, which must be paid in GBP at the time of submission and changes with exchange rates.

documents.name: Family relationship certificates for accompanying dependants
documents.description: Only if family members apply with you: civil-registry birth or marriage certificates, civil-partnership registration or other proof of an unregistered partnership; for adult children, proof of economic dependency and civil status; for ascendants, proof they are dependent on the teleworker. All apostilled and translated.

documents.name: Certificado / volante de empadronamiento from your Spanish town hall
documents.description: Municipal residence registration at the Ayuntamiento of your Spanish address, normally evidenced by a Spanish rental contract or property deed plus passport. Required for the TIE appointment and for most later administrative steps; it must generally be less than three months old when presented.

documents.name: TIE application: form EX-17 with tasa modelo 790 código 012
documents.description: Physical foreigner's identity card must be applied for in person within one month of entering Spain, at the Oficina de Extranjería or National Police station of your province, by prior appointment booked online. Bring the signed EX-17, passport plus copy, a colour passport photo on white background, empadronamiento and the paid 790/012 fee slip; fingerprints are taken at the appointment and the card is collected in person weeks later.

documents.name: Extranjería/Police appointment confirmation (cita previa)
documents.description: Booking confirmation obtained through the government electronic office for the fingerprinting and card-collection appointments; appointments are compulsory and may be issued several weeks out, so book immediately on arrival.

documents.name: Spanish tax and social security registration file
documents.description: Registration with the Agencia Tributaria (modelo 036/037 census declaration for freelancers) and, where you fall under the Spanish system rather than a UK A1, affiliation and enrolment with the Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social to obtain your social security number. Employees covered by a UK A1 should file the certificate instead — confirm your own case, as treatment differs between employees and self-employed.
documents.source: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) / Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social

documents.name: Modelo 149 application for the special expat tax regime
documents.description: Optional election of the 'Beckham Law' special non-resident tax regime available to international teleworkers, filed with the Agencia Tributaria within six months of the start of Spanish social security cover. Deadlines are strict; verify eligibility with AEAT or a Spanish tax adviser.

documents.name: Residence authorisation for international teleworker (renewal application to UGE-CE)
documents.description: The consular visa is valid for a maximum of one year; to continue living in Spain you must apply in Spain, within the 60 calendar days before the visa expires, for the autorización de residencia para teletrabajador de carácter internacional, evidencing that the original conditions (income, remote employment, insurance, clean record) still hold. Handled by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos.
documents.source: Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos (UGE-CE), Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones

documents.name: Evidence of effective residence in Spain for renewal
documents.description: For renewals and any later long-term residence application, keep proof of actual physical residence (padrón history, utility bills, tenancy, travel records, Spanish tax returns). Absences of more than six months in a year can jeopardise renewal — confirm the exact rule applicable to your case with the Oficina de Extranjería or UGE-CE.
documents.source: Oficina de Extranjería / Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones

documents.name: Indian passport (original, minimum 6 months validity)
documents.description: Machine-readable Indian passport valid at least 6 months beyond the intended entry date; used for the freelance permit/licence application, entry permit and Emirates ID file. Passport must have blank pages for stamping and details must exactly match all other documents.

documents.name: Coloured passport data-page scan (PDF/JPEG) for online upload
documents.description: High-resolution digital copy of the passport bio-data page uploaded to the ICP portal, GDRFA Dubai portal or free-zone e-portal. This is separate from presenting the original passport at biometric/medical appointments.

documents.name: Recent passport-size photographs (white background, UAE specification)
documents.description: Digital and printed colour photos of the applicant with white background, per UAE immigration photo specification. Required for the freelance permit file and again for the medical fitness/Emirates ID registration; these are photographs of the applicant, not photocopies of the passport.

documents.name: Bachelor's degree or specialised diploma (original certificate)
documents.description: Original Indian degree or specialised diploma proving the qualification required for the freelance/self-employment Green Residency route; the field should reasonably align with the declared freelance activity.

documents.name: Legalisation chain for the Indian degree (state HRD/SDM → MEA → UAE Embassy/Consulate in India)
documents.description: Because the UAE is not an Apostille-accepting state for these purposes, the Indian degree must be state-verified, then attested/apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs, then attested by the UAE Embassy in New Delhi or the UAE Consulates (Mumbai/Hyderabad/Thiruvananthapuram) per jurisdiction. Complete this in India before departure; formats have moved to digital attestation letters — verify current procedure with the UAE Embassy in India.
documents.source: Embassy of the UAE in New Delhi / Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

documents.name: Curriculum vitae and professional portfolio / client evidence
documents.description: Up-to-date CV plus samples, contracts or client references demonstrating the freelance activity applied for. Free zones and MOHRE assess the requested activity against this evidence before issuing the permit.

documents.name: Proof of self-employment income of at least AED 360,000 per year for the previous two years
documents.description: Invoices, client contracts, Indian income tax returns (ITR) or audited/certified income statements evidencing annual self-employment income of not less than AED 360,000 (or foreign-currency equivalent) for each of the two preceding years, for the Green Residency freelancer category.

documents.name: Proof of financial solvency (personal bank statements)
documents.description: Alternative to the income threshold: bank statements or a bank-issued balance/solvency certificate showing sufficient funds to support yourself throughout the residency period. This is the solvency evidence, distinct from the historical income evidence above; accepted formats and minimum balances are set by the issuing authority (ICP / GDRFA / ADRO) — verify with the relevant authority.

documents.name: Freelance / self-employment permit or free-zone freelancer licence
documents.description: The core authorisation: either a freelance work permit issued by the UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) or a freelancer/sole-professional licence from a recognised free zone (e.g. Dubai Development Authority, UAQ FTZ). Residency cannot be processed without it, and it names the permitted activity.

documents.name: eMigrate emigration clearance (ECR-category Indian passport holders only)
documents.description: The UAE is a notified ECR destination: Indian passport holders whose passport bears an ECR endorsement require emigration clearance from the Protector of Emigrants via eMigrate before departure. Graduate freelancers normally hold ECNR status and are exempt — check the ECR/ECNR page of your passport.
documents.source: Protector of Emigrants / eMigrate, Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

documents.name: Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) from Indian authorities, attested
documents.description: Character certificate issued by the Regional Passport Office or state police, legalised through the MEA and UAE Embassy chain. Not universally demanded for the freelancer Green Residency route but requested by some free zones and some emirates — verify with the specific issuing authority before paying for attestation.
documents.source: Passport Seva, Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

documents.name: Establishment card (immigration establishment/company card)
documents.description: Immigration card issued to the freelance licence holder that links the licence to the UAE immigration system and enables the entry permit and residence file. Typically arranged by the free zone or MOHRE-linked channel after the permit is issued.
documents.source: General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) Dubai / ICP

documents.name: Entry permit (e-visa) or in-country status change approval
documents.description: Electronic entry permit issued by ICP or GDRFA that allows entry to complete residency formalities; if already inside the UAE on another status, an in-country status change is used instead. GDRFA Dubai advises existing residents not to cancel current residency until the self-employment permit is issued.

documents.name: Medical fitness certificate for residency
documents.description: Mandatory screening (blood test and, in Dubai/Abu Dhabi, chest X-ray) at a government-approved centre — Emirates Health Services centres in the northern emirates, DHA-approved centres in Dubai — after receiving the entry permit and before Emirates ID issuance and residency activation. Bring the entry permit copy and passport.

documents.name: Emirates ID application and biometric enrolment record
documents.description: Biometric capture (fingerprints and facial image) and ICP Emirates ID application; the issued Emirates ID card is the primary residency credential, as residency is now linked digitally to the Emirates ID rather than a passport sticker.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: UAE health insurance policy in the applicant's own name
documents.description: Valid UAE-compliant medical insurance is a condition for residence issuance and renewal; self-sponsored freelancers must purchase and pay for their own policy meeting the minimum benefits of the emirate of residence (DHA in Dubai, DOH in Abu Dhabi).

documents.name: Registered tenancy contract (Ejari in Dubai / Tawtheeq in Abu Dhabi)
documents.description: Officially registered lease in the freelancer's name, needed to prove address for utility connections, dependant sponsorship, some bank accounts and school registration. Registration authority differs by emirate.
documents.source: Dubai Land Department (Ejari) / Abu Dhabi Department of Municipalities and Transport (Tawtheeq)

documents.name: UAE bank account opening file (licence + Emirates ID + residence proof)
documents.description: Resident/business account application supported by the freelance licence, establishment card, Emirates ID, passport with residence, and address proof. Needed to receive client payments locally and to evidence ongoing solvency at renewal; documentary requirements vary by bank under Central Bank KYC rules.

documents.name: Federal Tax Authority registrations (corporate tax; VAT if turnover exceeds threshold)
documents.description: Licensed freelancers are treated as conducting business activity and may need corporate tax registration, plus mandatory VAT registration once taxable turnover exceeds AED 375,000. Confirm your specific obligation and deadlines with the Federal Tax Authority.

documents.name: Annual freelance permit/licence renewal file
documents.description: Freelance permits and free-zone freelancer licences are generally issued for one year and must be renewed annually (residence itself may run longer, e.g. 5-year Green Residency); renewal requires an active licence, valid insurance and continued eligibility evidence.

documents.name: Attested marriage certificate and children's birth certificates (for dependant sponsorship)
documents.description: Indian-issued marriage and birth certificates legalised through the state authority, MEA and UAE Embassy chain, plus final UAE MOFAIC attestation, if you later sponsor a spouse, children or parents as a self-sponsored permit holder.
documents.source: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFAIC) attestation service / Embassy of the UAE in New Delhi

documents.name: Brazilian passport (original, valid)
documents.description: Original Brazilian passport with validity beyond the intended stay and blank pages for the visa vignette. VFS Global Brazil retains the original passport for the entire analysis period, so plan travel accordingly.

documents.name: Photocopy of passport biographic data page
documents.description: Plain photocopy of the biographic/photo page of the passport, submitted as a separate item in the D8 checklist (distinct from the original passport).

documents.name: Signed national visa application form (Formulário de Pedido de Visto)
documents.description: Portuguese national (non-Schengen) visa form, completed in full and signed in the designated signature field; must be signed in field 37 and at the end of the form per the Brazil checklist.

documents.name: Two identical biometric photos of the applicant (3x4 cm)
documents.description: Two recent identical photos of the applicant in consular standard, one of which is glued onto the application form; face must be unobstructed (no hats, hair covering, earrings) or the file will be rejected. Photos can also be taken at the VFS centre on the appointment day.

documents.name: Criminal record certificate from Brazilian Federal Police with Hague Apostille
documents.description: Atestado de Antecedentes Criminais issued by the Polícia Federal, issued within the last 30 days and apostilled. VFS Brazil states this must carry the Hague Apostille for all applicants regardless of nationality; some consular posts note it is the only document requiring apostille and is valid 90 days.

documents.name: Additional foreign criminal record certificate (if resident abroad in the last year)
documents.description: If the applicant lived in a country other than Brazil during the past year, a criminal record certificate from that country's competent authority, with Hague Apostille or legalisation, is also required.

documents.name: Authorisation for AIMA/SEF to consult Portuguese criminal record
documents.description: Signed consent form allowing Portuguese authorities to check the applicant's criminal record in Portugal; applicants under 16 are exempt from criminal-record documentation.

documents.name: Proof of remote work relationship (employment declaration or service/freelance contract)
documents.description: For employees, an employer declaration proving the employment relationship; for self-employed applicants, contracts or partnership/service agreements with clients based outside Portugal. The visa is for remote work contracted with any country except Portugal.

documents.name: Proof of means of subsistence (income + savings bank statements)
documents.description: Bank statements and/or payslips showing the legally set monthly income threshold (four times the Portuguese minimum wage) plus the required savings balance. Exact euro amounts change annually with the Portuguese minimum wage — verify the current portaria figure with the consular post before submitting.

documents.name: Brazilian tax residence document (comprovante de residência fiscal)
documents.description: Document attesting the applicant's fiscal residence, listed explicitly on the Brazil D8 checklist (e.g. Receita Federal tax residence proof / income tax declaration).

documents.name: Proof of address in Brazil (comprovante de residência)
documents.description: Full Brazilian address proof (street, number, complement, CEP, city, state) used to route the file to the consular post with jurisdiction over the applicant.

documents.name: Proof of accommodation in Portugal
documents.description: Signed lease, property deed, or host/accommodation declaration covering the stay in Portugal. Junta de Freguesia address attestations are not accepted by AIMA later in the process.

documents.name: Travel/health insurance valid in Portugal
documents.description: Insurance covering medical expenses, urgent care and repatriation in Portugal for the duration of the stay. Coverage minimums differ by consular post — confirm the required amount on the current checklist.

documents.name: Return transport ticket to Brazil
documents.description: Copy of return travel document (passagem de retorno ao Brasil) required on the Brazilian D8 temporary-stay checklist.

documents.name: Printed VFS checklist in duplicate with completed header
documents.description: Two copies of the specific D8 checklist with the applicant's header filled in; documents must be presented loose, in checklist order, single-sided A4, no staples or clips, or the file will not be accepted.

documents.name: Proof of legal entry into Portugal (PSP/GNR entry record or stamp)
documents.description: Evidence of the date of legal entry into national territory, to be presented at the AIMA appointment; entry declaration from PSP/GNR is preferred where no passport stamp exists.

documents.name: Portuguese tax number registration proof (NIF from Autoridade Tributária)
documents.description: Declaration from the Portuguese tax authority stating the applicant's NIF, required at the AIMA residence-permit appointment.

documents.name: Portuguese social security number registration proof (NISS)
documents.description: Social Security registration declaration showing the NISS, required where applicable — typically for self-employed/freelance D8 holders who register activity in Portugal. Verify applicability to your work arrangement with AIMA.

documents.name: AIMA residence permit application form plus accommodation evidence package
documents.description: Signed AIMA application form submitted in person at a Loja AIMA by appointment, accompanied by accommodation proof: for owners, the certidão de registo predial or its access code; for tenants, a landlord/host declaration stating the legal basis of use, and where the applicant's name is not on the contract, a sworn honour declaration plus an AT fiscal-domicile certificate issued less than 30 days earlier.

documents.name: Renewal file for the temporary residence permit (updated D8 evidence)
documents.description: For renewal via AIMA's Portal das Renovações: updated remote work contract/employer declaration, current income evidence, updated accommodation proof, and consent for criminal record consultation. Document lists are updated periodically — confirm on the AIMA portal at renewal time.

documents.name: Tax and social security compliance certificates (nada consta)
documents.description: Certificates from the Autoridade Tributária and Segurança Social confirming no outstanding obligations, required for permanent residence and commonly requested at renewal.

documents.name: Proof of basic Portuguese language knowledge (A2)
documents.description: Certificate from an official Portuguese teaching establishment or recognised A2 exam certificate, required when applying for permanent residence after five years of temporary residence.

documents.name: Nationality eligibility confirmation against the ISA list of eligible countries/regions
documents.description: CRITICAL BLOCKER: Japan's Digital Nomad status (Designated Activities, Ministry of Justice Notification No. 53) is limited to nationals of countries/regions holding BOTH a tax treaty and a visa-exemption arrangement with Japan (approx. 49-50 countries/regions). The People's Republic of China (ordinary PRC passport) is NOT on this list because PRC passport holders do not have visa-exempt entry to Japan, so a mainland Chinese citizen cannot obtain this visa. Holders of HKSAR, Macao SAR or Taiwan travel documents ARE on the eligible list. Print the current ISA eligible-countries PDF and verify your exact travel document before spending money on any other document. Verify with the Embassy of Japan in China, as the list is periodically updated.

documents.name: Eligible passport (HKSAR / Macao SAR / Taiwan travel document, or other eligible nationality)
documents.description: Original passport valid for the full intended stay (consulates commonly ask for 6 months' remaining validity beyond the visa expiry) with at least one to two completely blank visa pages. A mainland PRC ordinary passport cannot be used for this visa category; if you hold a PRC passport only, the practical alternatives are a Temporary Visitor visa (max 90 days, no work), an Engineer/Specialist in Humanities work visa, Highly Skilled Professional, or Business Manager/Startup status.

documents.name: Completed MOFA visa application form (Designated Activities)
documents.description: Official Japanese visa application form, completed in ink or typed (never pencil), signed, including a Japan-reachable contact telephone number. Some Japanese missions accept submission through the Japan e-Visa system instead of paper.

documents.name: Biometric passport photograph of the applicant (45mm x 45mm)
documents.description: One recent colour photo taken within the last 6 months, plain background, affixed to the visa application form. This is physically separate from any passport photocopy — both are typically requested.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan

documents.name: Photocopy of passport bio-data page and any current visas/residence stamps
documents.description: Plain paper copy of the identification page (and, if applying from a third country, of the pages showing your legal status there). Kept by the mission as the file copy; distinct from the original passport and from the biometric photo.
documents.source: Embassy of Japan in the People's Republic of China

documents.name: Proof of legal residence in the consulate's jurisdiction
documents.description: Residence permit, ID card, recent utility bill, bank statement or lease showing your full name and current address, proving the Japanese Embassy/Consulate-General you apply to has jurisdiction over you. Especially relevant for Chinese nationals residing abroad who hold an eligible second nationality or SAR travel document.

documents.name: Application submitted via a Japan-accredited visa agency (mainland China applicants)
documents.description: Japanese diplomatic missions in mainland China generally do not accept walk-in individual visa applications; files must be lodged through an accredited/designated travel or visa agency, which issues a submission receipt you should retain. Confirm the current agency list and whether the Designated Activities category is handled this way with your jurisdictional Japanese mission before filing.
documents.source: Embassy of Japan in the People's Republic of China

documents.name: Description of Intended Activities in Japan (ISA prescribed form)
documents.description: Statement on the ISA form describing the remote work you will perform, the overseas employer/clients, the timeframe, and your contact details including a phone number reachable in Japan. Required only when applying WITHOUT a Certificate of Eligibility.

documents.name: Proof of annual income of at least JPY 10,000,000
documents.description: Chinese individual income tax payment record (个人所得税纳税记录) from the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau, or salary/dividend statements and audited business income for the self-employed, showing at least JPY 10 million in the year of application from non-Japanese sources. Provide a Japanese or English translation; some missions require notarisation.

documents.name: Remote-work employment contract or overseas client contracts
documents.description: Contract with a company incorporated outside Japan, or freelance/consulting agreements and invoices with non-Japan-based clients, confirming the work is performed remotely. Contracts with Japanese companies or invoicing of Japanese entities is prohibited under this status and will cause refusal.

documents.name: Private medical insurance certificate with JPY 10,000,000+ coverage
documents.description: Copy of the policy plus an insurer-issued coverage certificate in English or Japanese, covering death, injury and illness in Japan for the entire stay, with a minimum indemnity of JPY 10 million and coverage for rescue/repatriation costs. Digital Nomad holders cannot enrol in Japanese National Health Insurance, so this is the sole health cover.

documents.name: Certificate of Eligibility (COE) issued by a Regional Immigration Bureau
documents.description: Optional advance approval filed in Japan by a proxy. If presented at the visa application, the separate income-proof, insurance and planned-activity documents may be omitted. Processing can take around three months, so most applicants apply directly at the mission instead.

documents.name: Notarised family relationship documents for accompanying spouse/children
documents.description: For dependants applying under Designated Activities Notification No. 54: Chinese marriage certificate (结婚证) and/or birth certificate (出生医学证明), notarised and translated, plus a copy of the principal digital nomad's passport and separate insurance for each family member. Legally recognised marriage and cohabitation are required; de-facto and same-sex partnerships are not covered.

documents.name: Visit Japan Web pre-registration QR codes
documents.description: Online pre-registration for immigration entry and customs declaration completed before boarding; generates QR codes presented at the airport to speed up landing procedures.
documents.source: Visit Japan Web, Digital Agency of Japan

documents.name: Landing permission seal granting Designated Activities (Digital Nomad), 6 months
documents.description: Granted in the passport at the port of entry; the visa itself is single-entry and valid only 3 months from issue, so you must enter within that window. Note that Digital Nomad holders are not mid-to-long-term residents, so no Residence Card (在留カード) and no resident registration (住民票) are issued — keep the passport stamp as your only proof of status.

documents.name: Customs declaration for accompanied and unaccompanied personal effects
documents.description: Declaration form for baggage and any separately shipped belongings; submit the unaccompanied-baggage copy at arrival to clear items shipped from China duty-free as personal effects.

documents.name: Short-stay accommodation contract (monthly apartment, serviced flat or hotel)
documents.description: Signed booking or monthly-lease agreement covering the stay. Without a Residence Card most standard long-term Japanese leases, bank accounts and postpaid mobile contracts are unavailable, so arrange accommodation, eSIM/prepaid data and payment methods that do not require residency.

documents.name: Chinese Certificate of Tax Residency (中国税收居民身份证明)
documents.description: Issued by the State Taxation Administration to support treaty relief under the Japan-China double taxation agreement. Foreign-source income is generally not taxed in Japan under this status, but residency can be argued if your centre of living is in Japan — take professional advice for stays approaching 183 days.
documents.source: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China

documents.name: Special Re-entry Permit confirmation for trips out of Japan
documents.description: Digital Nomad holders may use the deemed re-entry permit system when leaving and returning within the validity of their stay; because no Residence Card is issued, confirm at the airport immigration counter which departure form and endorsement apply to your case before travelling.

documents.name: Departure or change-of-status file before the 6-month expiry
documents.description: The 6-month period cannot be extended or renewed. To stay in Japan you must file a Change of Status of Residence application (e.g. to Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Business Manager or Highly Skilled Professional) with supporting employer or company documents; otherwise you must depart, and re-application as a digital nomad generally requires around six consecutive months outside Japan.
